entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen23213" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen23214" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen23215" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen23215" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen23214" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen23216" type="x-p"/> An exhortation to praise God in his sanctuary, <reference osisRef="Psa.134.1-Psa.134.3">Psa 134:1-3</reference>. <div eID="gen23216" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23217" type="x-p"/> This is the last of the fifteen Psalms called Psalms of degrees. Who was the author is uncertain; it is attributed to David only by the Syriac; it is intimately connected with the two preceding Psalms, and is an exhortation to the priests and Levites who kept nightly watch in the temple, to the assiduous in praising the Lord. It seems to consist of two parts: 1. An exhortation, probably from the high priest, to those priests and Levites who kept watch in the temple by night, to spend their time profitably, and duly celebrate the praises of God, <reference osisRef="Psa.134.1">Psa 134:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Psa.134.2">Psa 134:2</reference>. The second part, which is contained in the <reference osisRef="Psa.134.3">Psa 134:3</reference>, is the prayer of the priests and Levites for the high priest, who seems now to be going to his rest. <div eID="gen23217" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23218" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen23218" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23219" type="x-p"/> Behold, bless ye the Lord - I believe הנה hinneh should be taken here in the sense of take heed! Be upon your guard; you serve a jealous God; provoke him not. <div eID="gen23219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23220" type="x-p"/> Which by night stand - Who minister during the night.
entries.content_plain: Introduction An exhortation to praise God in his sanctuary, Psa 134:1-3 . This is the last of the fifteen Psalms called Psalms of degrees. Who was the author is uncertain; it is attributed to David only by the Syriac; it is intimately connected with the two preceding Psalms, and is an exhortation to the priests and Levites who kept nightly watch in the temple, to the assiduous in praising the Lord. It seems to consist of two parts: 1. An exhortation, probably from the high priest, to those priests and Levites who kept watch in the temple by night, to spend their time profitably, and duly celebrate the praises of God, Psa 134:1 , Psa 134:2 . The second part, which is contained in the Psa 134:3 , is the prayer of the priests and Levites for the high priest, who seems now to be going to his rest. Verse 1 Behold, bless ye the Lord - I believe הנה hinneh should be taken here in the sense of take heed! Be upon your guard; you serve a jealous God; provoke him not. Which by night stand - Who minister during the night.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen23220" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23221" type="x-p"/> Lift up your hands in the sanctuary - קדש kodesh, "in holiness:" or, as the Syriac, lekoudishe, "to holiness;" in sancta, Vulgate; and εις τα ἁγια, Septuagint; "in holy things; or, as the Aethiopic, in the house of the sanctuary." The expression seems very similar to that of St. Paul, <reference osisRef="1Tim.2.8">1Tim 2:8</reference> : "Lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting." <div eID="gen23221" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23222" type="x-p"/> Bless the Lord - That is, speak good of his name: tell the wonders he has wrought, and show that his name is exalted.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen23222" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23223" type="x-p"/> The Lord that made heaven and earth - Who governs and possesses all things; and who can give you every spiritual and earthly blessing. <div eID="gen23223" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23224" type="x-p"/> Bless thee out of Zion - As if they had said, "We will attend to your orders; go in peace, and may God shower down his blessings upon you!" The blessing pronounced by the priests was the following: "The Lord bless thee and keep thee! The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and he gracious unto thee! The Lord lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace!" <reference osisRef="Num.6.24-Num.6.26">Num 6:24-26</reference>.  <chapter eID="Ps.134"/> <div eID="gen23224" type="x-p"/>
